title: Could you pay with a sandwich?
speech: Alex offers a sandwich for a notebook. The seller is not hungry. How does money solve this problem?

title: What is money?
speech: Money is anything generally accepted as a means of payment. Valuable is not enough: people must normally accept it. Common forms include notes, coins and bank deposits. A phone or card is a payment tool, not the money itself.

title: Medium of exchange
speech: Alex pays twenty yuan for a notebook. Money is a medium of exchange: it buys goods and services. The seller can spend it elsewhere, without wanting Alex's sandwich.

title: Unit of account
speech: Alex compares notebooks priced at twenty and thirty yuan. Money is a unit of account, or measure of value. A common unit lets him compare prices. No purchase is needed.

title: Store of value
speech: Alex saves one hundred yuan for next month's trip. Money is a store of value: it carries purchasing power into the future. Inflation can weaken this function because rising prices mean the same money buys less.

title: Standard of deferred payment
speech: Alex borrows fifty yuan and agrees to repay it next Friday. Money is a standard of deferred payment: future debts are expressed and settled in money. The clue is an agreed future payment, rather than simply saving.

title: Which function is being illustrated?
speech: Which functions do these examples show? A displayed price; an agreement to repay next month. Choose before the answers appear.

title: Price measurement versus a future debt
speech: The price shows unit of account. The repayment agreement shows standard of deferred payment. Identify the action, then name its function.

title: What would make good money?
speech: Functions are money's jobs. Characteristics are properties that help it perform those jobs. Remember these seven.

title: Durable: it lasts
speech: Durable: money lasts through repeated use. Ice cream melts; coins do not quickly perish. Durability supports saving, but physical durability does not guarantee stable purchasing power.

title: Portable: easy to carry
speech: Portable: money is easy to carry, making payments convenient. Notes fit in a pocket; a huge rock does not.

title: Divisible: useful smaller units
speech: Divisible: different denominations allow payments of different sizes. For a seven yuan sandwich, a ten yuan note gets three yuan change. Do not cut up banknotes.

title: Uniform: equal units are interchangeable
speech: Uniform: genuine notes of the same denomination have the same monetary value. Two ten yuan notes are interchangeable, even with different serial numbers.

title: Recognisable: easy to identify
speech: Recognisable: people can identify the currency and its value. Clear denominations and security features help them recognise genuine money.

title: Generally acceptable: people receive it
speech: Generally acceptable: people are willing to receive it in payment because others accept it too. This supports its medium of exchange function.

title: Limited in supply: not freely reproducible
speech: Limited in supply: money cannot be freely reproduced without limit. This helps maintain value. Limited does not mean its quantity never changes, and scarcity alone does not make something money.

title: Explain two characteristics of money. [4]
speech: Exam check: explain two characteristics of money. Four marks. Pause and write two explanations before continuing.

title: Two characteristics, each explained
speech: Money is portable: it is easy to carry when making payments. Money is divisible: different denominations allow payments of different values. Here, each characteristic and explanation earns two marks. Keep functions and characteristics distinct.
